stemMd: A laboratory uses 3 parts reagent for every 7 parts water by volume. Ignoring volume contraction, how much reagent is needed for 250 mL of mixture?
explanationMd: The mixture has 3 + 7 = 10 equal parts. Reagent accounts for 3/10 of the total, so its volume is 250 × 3/10 = 75 mL. The remaining 175 mL of water gives the required ratio 75:175 = 3:7.

distractorRationale.d: This treats the ratio as one reagent part out of ten.
distractorRationale.a: This gives a reagent fraction of two fifths, not three tenths.
distractorRationale.c: This applies the ratio 3/7 to total mixture rather than to water.
